chunks: To Pharaoh and his nobles who behaved with arrogance, for they were a conceited lot,
ai.seo_question: Who were the arrogant nobles that accompanied Pharaoh?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Al-Mu'minun, this verse characterizes Pharaoh and his elite not merely as political rulers but as a 'high-status' group whose arrogance stemmed from a sense of self-sufficiency, leading them to reject the divine message. Shia exegesis often highlights this 'istikbar' (arrogance) as a spiritual disease that blinds the elite to truth, contrasting their worldly elevation with their ultimate spiritual downfall.
